subject: New video shows trio of headlamp-wearing ‘mole people’ emerge from NYC manhole near Penn Station

Viral TikToks show thrill-seekers emerging from NYC sewers near Penn Station, alarming authorities and baffling commuters.
Evidence: viral novelty trend, extreme sewer hazard, illicit scavenging
#NYC #TikTok #Aletheia

Resulting Judgement: (-0.7, -0.6) — Lesser Evil

Context: TikTok clips show individuals climbing out of NYC manholes near Penn Station at 4 AM, prompting NYPD and DEP investigations into sewer scavenging.

The Poison:
Romanticizing illegal industrial trespassing as harmless adventure for online views, enticing others into deadly environments.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Plane Error (WHERE vs WHO): Treating a localized stunt as abstract digital content while ignoring physical subterranean dangers.

Social Physics Analysis:
Viral media incentives override basic survival instincts. Chasing online attention replaces transparent respect for municipal safety and laws.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. Clout-seeking masks severe physical risks.

The Unavoidable Truth: City sewers are toxic, unstable death traps unfit for casual treasure hunting.

The Unavoidable Lie: Viral manhole videos are harmless pranks without real safety consequences.
